original_test_intent: Read Redfish FirmwareInventory and prove that every intended GPU maps to the correct firmware component and approved firmware version for the installed GPU topology.
original_method: Verify SUT/BMC/GPU identities; perform TLS-validated authenticated GETs to the FirmwareInventory collection and members; map members by stable component/device identifiers rather than position; compare version against the approved per-GPU baseline; record missing, duplicate, ambiguous or mismatched entries without mutation.
manual_activity: Owner supplies the GPU topology, Redfish mapping and approved version list; agent performs read-only collection and comparison.
required_inputs: Verified BMC/SUT and installed GPU topology
Vendor FirmwareInventory schema and stable GPU member mapping
Protected Redfish credentials and TLS trust
safety_requirements: GET only; never invoke update actions or change firmware
Validate target and TLS and protect/redact credentials/tokens
Capture complete collection and each mapped member before normalization
Stop on ambiguous identity, incomplete data or endpoint mismatch
agent_execution_scope: Enumerate the collection and dereference relevant members
Map each installed GPU to stable inventory identity and compare versions
Preserve raw/redacted JSON, HTTP/TLS metadata and discrepancies
Do not use hardcoded insecure endpoint, guess mapping, update firmware or decide DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve topology-to-inventory mapping and required members
Review missing, ambiguous or mismatched evidence and decide verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The GET is read-only but its hardcoded HTTP address and sshpass/host-key bypass are not acceptable, and the collection alone may not contain member versions.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Query the verified HTTPS Redfish collection and every mapped GPU member with protected authentication, parse JSON structurally and compare to the approved matrix.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: FirmwareInventory resource, GPU firmware goal and 5/5-minute estimate remain; insecure transport and implicit user inspection are replaced.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a topology-aware inventory table from collection/member JSON and compare stable IDs and normalized versions to the approved baseline.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes hardcoded insecure access and adds member dereference, identity, completeness and exact oracle.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A readable collection does not prove the intended GPU is present or that its version is correct.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware names and versions may be vendor-formatted or aggregated; mapping rules must be approved rather than inferred.

project_override_considerations: If one inventory member represents a GPU tray/baseboard rather than each GPU, document the approved aggregation rule and preserve installed-device coverage. Missing Redfish exposure is a finding, not permission to flash.
expected_evidence: SUT/BMC/GPU topology and approved version matrix
TLS/HTTP status and complete redacted collection/member JSON
Stable GPU-to-member mapping and normalized version comparison
Missing/duplicate/ambiguous member report, timestamps, no-mutation audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title, procedure and Criteria consistently request a read-only GPU firmware inventory check. The exact baseline and secure endpoint are absent prerequisites/oracles rather than contradictory source coverage.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The read-only method is executable when the normal Redfish access, mapping and expected-version inputs are available.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2257 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00039-V001: approve BMC/SUT/GPU topology, Redfish FirmwareInventory collection/member schema and stable mapping for every intended GPU; provide the approved firmware version/compatibility matrix and normalization/aggregation rules; approve verified HTTPS/TLS and protected authentication, complete-member evidence and handling of missing, duplicate or ambiguous entries.

review_improvement: Keeps the fully automatable read-only scope while turning a raw collection dump into exact GPU identity and firmware-version evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A FirmwareInventory collection is a directory, not necessarily the component data itself. GPU firmware may appear in member resources with vendor naming, shared controllers or multiple devices. A hardcoded internal HTTP endpoint can query the wrong BMC and exposes authentication context. Reliable automation therefore requires target identity, complete member enumeration, stable GPU mapping and an approved version matrix; no human visual confirmation is intrinsically required once those inputs exist.
